properties.name: A session can find out what designs exist nearby and be told which one to use, rather than inheriting one from where the shell happened to be
properties.statement:
Which design a session writes to must be a STATED CHOICE, and the information needed to make that choice must be available BEFORE anything is created. Two halves: (1) an agent must be able to discover what designs exist in and around a working tree and what each one holds — label, size, when it was minted — without opening a session against each; (2) a session must be able to be pointed at a chosen design explicitly.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-05, after the hxm_program field report: "can we just pass the location of the reflow2 graph via a prompt or skill; it can default to whichever folder path that the session is opened in, but maybe we could just say 'use reflow2 graph as /path/to/reflow2/graph/to/use/for/this/session'." And on the mechanism, once told a skill could not do it alone: "I like this approach of just pointing .mcp.json at the graph_id... an agent within a session can usually change files. can a reflow2 tool be to simply return all graph_ids to the agent and the agent then can choose whichever graph_id the user specifies to use for the project?"

WHY IT IS A REQUIREMENT AND NOT A CONVENIENCE. Today the answer is implicit: the launch config passes a RELATIVE `--graph-path`, so the design a session edits is decided by where the shell was opened, with no ancestor walk and no report of what else exists. Measured consequence, on Anthony's own repo the same day: a session at the root was told "this directory has no design yet" and minted a THIRD graph while two populated ones sat one and two directories down (`dec:no-design-here-never-looked`). An implicit answer to "which design am I editing" is not a smaller version of an explicit one — it is the mechanism by which a design gets created in the wrong place and nobody is told.

THE DIVISION OF LABOUR THIS INHERITS, and it shapes the answer rather than limiting it: reflow2 performs NO FILE IO (`dec:agent-navigates-content`), so WALKING THE TREE TO FIND `.reflow2` DIRECTORIES IS THE AGENT'S JOB — Anthony's own observation that "an agent within a session can usually change files" is the same point from the other side. What only reflow2 can answer is what a store at a given path actually HOLDS. So the requirement is met by a pair, not by one tool.

⚠️ MEASURED, AND IT CORRECTS THE OBVIOUS READING OF THE ASK: "return all graph_ids" would return ONE per store today. Storage keys are `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}` and `dynograph_storage::keys::graph_prefix` exists, so many graphs per store is supported by the FOUNDATION — but reflow2 opens one graph per store by convention (`DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID`, one `.reflow2` directory per project), and the three graphs in this field report are three separate STORES. Enumerating within a store is therefore true and not useful yet; describing a store found on disk is what the case actually needs.

HOW EACH HALF STANDS, 2026-08-05. HALF (1) — DISCOVERY — has an accepted shape and a planned capability: `dec:describe-a-design-without-binding-to-it` and `cap:describe-design-at-path`. HALF (2) — BEING POINTED — has a WORKING ANSWER IN THE FIELD but not a settled one: `dec:pointing-a-session-is-project-scope-only` (accepted, executed and verified on hxm_program) says a project-scoped config override does it TODAY, with the hard rule that an absolute path must never enter a global config. Whether that remains the answer, or a graph reference carried per call replaces it, is still open at `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`.

⚠️ AND THE REASON THIS REQUIREMENT IS NOT ALREADY MET BY THE FIELD FIX: PROJECT SCOPE KEYS ON THE DIRECTORY THE SESSION WAS OPENED IN. An override on a project root does nothing for a session opened in a subdirectory — which is precisely the case that produced the extra graph. So the config override satisfies this requirement for sessions started at the root and NOT OTHERWISE, and the discovery half stays necessary rather than being made redundant by it.

ACCEPTED 2026-08-05 on Anthony's explicit word ("Let's take req:a-session-chooses-its-design from proposed to accepted"), given after both halves and the surviving limitation above were read back to him.
